claims.statement: CTIS makes trial identifiers, therapeutic area, sponsor details and recruitment or trial dates publicly viewable, and revised transparency rules have applied since June 2024.
ABM reported that the CTIS map contained 1,945 trials at 1,251 Polish sites as of 22 May 2025, providing enough records for a Poland-focused entity-resolution wedge.
Normalized competition and site-identity intelligence will improve feasibility decisions enough to command protocol-level fees.

contrary_evidence: EMA already provides a public trial portal and multilingual clinical-trial map.
Public CTIS records do not establish site enrollment speed, data quality, investigator availability or budget.
Large CROs and sponsors already own feasibility systems and private performance data.

economics.acquisition_route: Approach CRO feasibility leads and Polish Clinical Trials Support Centres with one high-quality therapeutic-area sample; use direct written outreach and partner referrals rather than conferences or a personal brand.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A maintained site-identity graph and tracked changes can reduce repeated cleaning. Public CTIS data does not reveal enrollment performance, so any stronger ranking requires customer-supplied outcomes and must be validated rather than presumed.
fingerprint.customer: Small and midsize CRO business-development teams, sponsors and clinical-trial site networks choosing Polish or CEE sites for a new protocol.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Approach CRO feasibility leads and Polish Clinical Trials Support Centres with one high-quality therapeutic-area sample; use direct written outreach and partner referrals rather than conferences or a personal brand.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Resolve public CTIS sponsors and site names, map therapeutic areas and recruitment windows, show competition density and evidence provenance, and deliver a ranked research pack that clearly separates public facts from inferred site fit. Start with analyst reports, then subscription data.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A CRO or sponsor pays for a protocol-specific country and site landscape before outreach; a site network can subscribe to therapeutic-area and competitor alerts.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A protocol enters country and site feasibility, and teams need to see competing active trials, sponsor patterns, recruitment status and normalized site identities before sending broad questionnaires.

founder_fit: Combines health, neuroscience and entity-resolution skills
Public-data report can be built and tested part-time
High-value B2B deliverables may support a small customer count
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: Poland and CEE clinical-trial site feasibility intelligence
uncertainties: Permitted and technically stable method for repeated structured extraction
Accuracy of site entity resolution across languages and sponsor-entered names
Which small CRO or sponsor segment lacks incumbent tooling
Price and procurement cycle for protocol-specific reports
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: For one therapeutic area, manually verify a 25-site Poland and CEE landscape and show it to five CRO feasibility or site-network leads. Ask for a paid report tied to one upcoming protocol; do not build a platform unless at least one buyer pays and identifies a decision changed by the evidence.
